claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
A 5 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating is applied to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 coating will reduce the oxidation rate.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Reducing oxidation with the coating will preserve useful room-temperature mechanical performance.
Reducing oxidation with the coating will preserve useful high-temperature mechanical performance.
At 800 °C in air for 100 h, the coating will reduce oxidation rate by 50% relative to uncoated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will result in a 20% increase in yield strength at 1000 °C relative to untreated material.
Coating quality, thickness, uniformity, and test conditions may affect the achieved oxidation-rate reduction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 50% oxidation-rate reduction and a 20% yield-strength increase, but the falsification rule accepts reductions as low as 30% and strength increases as low as 10%. Thus, results that fail the stated quantitative prediction would not falsify the hypothesis under its own rule.

The stated boundary specifies 800 °C, whereas the mechanical outcome is yield strength at 1000 °C; the hypothesis does not clarify whether this is measured during exposure, after an 800 °C exposure, or under a separate 1000 °C test.
